newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank seen leaving German rates on hold.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank seen leaving German rates on hold.

text.p: The Bundesbank, satisfied that the German economy is recovering without inflation, will leave interest rates unchanged at its council meeting Thursday, analysts forecast.
All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters Tuesday said the German central bank would keep rates on hold and only one predicted that there would be another cut in the discount and Lombard rates this year.
"We expect a clear improvement in the economy during the year," said Petra Koehler, economist at Dresdner Bank. "A cut in rates would not give any help."
All of the surveyed economists said they expected the Bundesbank to leave its key money market rate, the securities repurchase rate, fixed at three percent.
Earlier on Tuesday the Federal Statistics Office reported that consumer prices rose 1.5 percent year-on-year in March, down from a 1.7 percent pace in February.

Industrial output, which climbed 7.1 percent year-on-year in February, up from January's two percent annual growth rate, shows that the economy is picking up without additional monetary stimulation, economists said.
"The economy is recovering and there is still no inflation risk -- so there is no need for a rate reduction at the moment," said Alison Cottrell, economist at PaineWebber in London.
The Bundesbank last cut the discount and Lombard rates almost exactly a year ago to 2.50 and 4.50 percent, respectively.
